topics.label: Introduction to the lecture
topics.groupedBecause: These opening remarks welcome students and outline the core aims and comparative focus of the lecture on cancer therapy.

topics.label: Traditional cancer treatments and cytotoxic chemotherapy
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics cover traditional treatment modalities including surgery, radiotherapy, and cytotoxic chemotherapy, detailing their mechanisms of action and significant systemic limitations.

topics.label: Exploiting intrinsic vulnerabilities and genetic defects in cancer cells
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine targeted strategies that exploit specific cancer cell vulnerabilities, including hormone-dependent signaling, cell cycle checkpoint deficiencies, and impaired DNA repair pathways.

topics.label: Kinase inhibitors, oncogene addiction, and mechanisms of resistance
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics discuss the design and clinical application of small-molecule kinase inhibitors against oncogenic drivers, as well as the emergence of drug resistance, bypass signaling, and drug addiction.

topics.label: Monoclonal antibody therapies and antibody-drug conjugates
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explore antibody-based therapeutics that either disrupt cell-surface receptor signaling, trigger immune effector mechanisms, or deliver targeted cytotoxic agents.

topics.label: Cancer immunotherapy and cellular immune targeting
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics evaluate the principles of immune surveillance and the implementation of immunotherapies, including immune checkpoint inhibitors, bispecific antibodies, and CAR T-cell therapies.

topics.label: Current challenges, clinical trends, and future directions in cancer therapy
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics address broader perspectives on cancer management, including tumor heterogeneity, genomic stratification, historical survival trends, and ethical considerations surrounding treatment options.
